From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Lee <samantha@brightai.com>
Date: Wed, 24 Jun 2026 15:05:00 -0700
Subject: Availability credit structure for BrightAI pilot

Hi Samantha —

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. Per our conversation, I wanted to outline a simple availability / credit structure that we can include in the pilot SOW so your procurement team can review. High-level ask from BrightAI was: clear uptime tiers, a predictable crediting formula, and a small retainer to get guaranteed escalation coverage.

Draft (pilot):
- Commitment: 6-month pilot, committed capacity pool (dedicated GPU) at agreed throughput.
- Uptime tiers and credits (monthly): 99.95%+ — no credit; 99.9%–99.949% — 2% credit of monthly invoice; 99.5%–99.899% — 5% credit; <99.5% — 10% credit + remediation plan.
- Retainer: optional 8-hour/month technical retainer (covers 1x expedited incident response within 4 hours + up to 2 deep-dive follow-ups).
- Discounting: pilot introductory discount is negotiable — we can offer a term-limited concession instead of permanent list-price reduction.

Attaching a short PDF that maps these tiers to example invoice lines so procurement can model economics. If this looks reasonable, I can convert into a short SOW and DocuSign link.

Best,
Karthik
Karthik Iyer | Account Executive, Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0123

Thanks, Karthik —

This is helpful. A couple of follow-ups from procurement and engineering:
- Can you confirm credits apply to invoices for the region where our production traffic runs (us-west-2)?
- We need a stronger first-year commercial concession to get internal sign-off — procurement is asking for a 30% discount on the pilot monthly fee (or equivalent crediting). Is that something Redwood will consider for a 6-month pilot if we commit to a 12–18 month follow-on?
- For response times, can the retainer guarantee an acknowledged incident within 1 hour and on-call engagement within 4 hours? We’ll need the escalation chain documented for our SOC and procurement review.

I’ve looped in procurement (procurement@brightai.com) who will expect a formal SOW and PO once terms are agreed.

Appreciate it —
Samantha
Samantha Lee | Head of Platform, BrightAI
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 25 Jun 2026 09:10:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Availability credit structure for BrightAI pilot — pricing ask (internal)

Laura / Marissa —

Looping you for pricing and approvals. BrightAI is pushing hard for a 30% pilot concession tied to a follow-on commit. They also want a faster acknowledgment SLA on the retainer (1hr). My read: BrightAI is a mid-sized vendor with good upsell potential (observed usage during demo). Options I see:

1) Concession + structured credits (low credits, but 20% one-time pilot credit applied to first invoice). Retainer remains 8 hrs/mo, acknowledgement within 1hr for Severity 1, on-call engagement within 4hrs.
2) Permanent % discount (we prefer to avoid). Offer a 15% first-year discount + 5% thereafter if they commit to 12 months post-pilot. Keep credits as proposed.
3) No list-price discount, but enhanced credit ladder and a refundable retainer that applies to incident hours beyond allotment.

Recommended: route (2) — gives commercial concession without de-anchoring list price, shows willingness to commit, and is easiest for renewals. If we do (2) we should add a cap on monthly credit payouts (e.g., credits capped at 50% of monthly committed spend) and a max of one accelerated-oncall incident per month under the retainer.

Thoughts? I can draft a short SOW + DocuSign template if this approach is OK.

— Karthik

Hi Samantha —

Thanks — below is a concrete proposal we can put in the SOW and send to DocuSign. I pulled in Laura for legal/pricing sign-off; Marissa is aware of the discussion.

Proposal (pilot SOW highlights):
- Term: 6 months pilot; BrightAI commits to a quarterly business review and provides estimated monthly tokens/throughput.
- Pricing concession: 15% off list for month 1–6 (introductory pilot concession), 5% recurring discount (months 7–18) if BrightAI signs 12-month follow-on within 60 days of pilot end.
- Uptime credit table (monthly):
   • 99.95% and above — no credit
   • 99.90% — 2% credit
   • 99.50%–99.89% — 5% credit
   • Below 99.50% — 10% credit + mandatory remediation plan and optional service credit up to additional 10% with mutual review
- Credit caps: monthly credits capped at 50% of monthly committed spend. Credits are applied to the next invoice.
- Retainer: 8 hours/month technical retainer — includes 1x expedited incident response (acknowledgment within 1 hour, on-call engagement within 4 hours) per month; additional incident-hours billed at standard hourly rates or drawn from the retainer balance.
- Escalation: named on-call contact + playbook link; Redwood agrees to provide SOC-friendly escalation ladder and runbook for procurement review.

Attachments: I’m attaching the SLA tiers doc with sample modeling. I’ll generate the SOW and DocuSign link once you confirm the concession number. If you need a higher concession, we can move to a 20% pilot-only concession but would request a firm written follow-on commitment or minimum spend (TBD).

If this looks reasonable I’ll send the SOW to procurement and include a short redline-friendly clause set for legal.

Best,
Karthik
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.com
